label: late original-phase steps of long sequences that open with l/r/i/n/s/a/x/g, boosted on k/u/3/m/b/p/v/1/j inputs
explanation: Behaves like a graded evidence accumulator, not a crisp detector. It fires almost only in the original phase (96% of mass) at late positions: never at t<=2, rising sharply with orig_idx (rate 0.5% at idx 4 up to 20% at idx 8). So it is mostly a feature of long sequences (L=9 holds 61% of mass), with a weaker echo on the <DEL> step (4% of mass). It never fires during the copy phase. Two content effects add to position. (1) Which tokens came earlier: it prefers sequences whose first tokens are from {l,r,i,n,s,a,x,g} (first_tok l/r/i lift about 3x), and the first two positions weigh most. (2) The current input: k, u, 3, m, b, p, v, 1, j raise the rate 2-4x. It also prefers first occurrences of a token (in_first lift 1.6x). The top activations are late steps (positions 6-8) carrying a boosting token like k/u/v in sequences that start with l/r/i. The recorded predicate is an additive score: position + count of earlier set-A tokens + extra weight for set-A tokens at positions 0-1 + a bonus for a boosting input. It captures about 83% of the activation mass on dev but has low precision (about 0.34), because the real unit is a soft linear combination that one threshold only approximates. The simple rule (late original step, orig_idx>=5) gets 0.90 recall but only 0.07 precision.
